To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
applied cultural semiotics is a viable and promising methodological approach for the resolution of complex culture-related problems in organizations and communities.

(1) cultural semiotics is an action research method; (2) action research is a cultural semiotic method; (3) both are systemic methods; (4) both are qualitative methods; (5) both are interpretive methods; and (6) both are creative methods.

the application of cultural semiotics to action-research is a powerful tool for the development of creative and innovative approaches to problem solving and knowledge management in the modern democratic policy making process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for the development of an “integrated approach” to knowledge production, knowledge transfer, and policy making.
the development of a new, more inclusive and participatory, approach to social and political problem solving in the information age.
the development of a new paradigm for applied cultural semiotics, one that is based on a systemic and action-oriented approach to the study of culture and organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the potential for applied cultural semiotics to contribute to the resolution of social issues lies in the capacity of its practitioners to develop a “sense-making” approach that is grounded in a systemic view of the culture-organization relationship, and that is capable of integrating the various perspectives of stakeholders and of the different levels of analysis involved in the problem-solving process.

applied cultural semiotics is not only an effective tool for the study and analysis of culture and organizations but also a powerful method for the design and implementation of intercultural policy and action-research projects.

cultural semiotics and its related fields of inquiry are a powerful tool for the analysis of complex culture-related issues and for the development of innovative solutions to the problems posed by the knowledge industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of cultural semiotics to the field of action-research is a promising new approach for the study of culture and its relation to social action.
the “systemic” approach to cultural semiotics and to action-research provides the conceptual framework and methodology to address the “wicked” problems in the knowledge age.

of “applied cultural semiotics,” which we define as the application of cultural semiotics to the analysis of complex social problems in order to facilitate the development of creative and innovative solutions to these problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cultural semiotics, when applied to social action research, provides the necessary theoretical framework and methodological tools for the implementation of a systemic approach to complex problem-solving processes.
cultural semiotics, as a qualitative method, is a powerful tool for social change and action-research.

cultural semiotics, in its applied form, provides a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between academic research and social policy making, thus contributing to the development of more inclusive and participatory modes of governance.
